question.text: Scenario: Mr. Vikram Mehta, aged 55, has Rs. 50 lakh to invest in fixed income instruments. He is considering two options: Bond A — AAA-rated corporate bond: Face value Rs. 100, Coupon rate 9% (annual payments), Remaining maturity 5 years, Current market price Rs. 104.10, Credit rating AAA. Bond B — Government Security: Face value Rs. 100, Coupon rate 7.5% (semi-annual payments), Remaining maturity 10 years, Current market price Rs. 95.50, Issued by Government of India. Additional information: The current 5-year G-Sec yield is 7.2%. The credit spread for AAA-rated corporate bonds over G-Secs is typically 80-100 basis points. The day count convention for Indian bonds is 30/360. Vikram wants to understand the yield, duration risk, and reinvestment risk of each option before making a decision. He plans to hold the bonds until maturity. Question 3 of 5: For Bond A trading at a premium, which of the following correctly orders the Coupon Rate (CR), Current Yield (CY), and Yield to Maturity (YTM)?

answer.text: Coupon rate is lower than current yield, and current yield is lower than YTM
Coupon rate is greater than current yield, and current yield is greater than YTM
Coupon rate, current yield, and YTM are all equal
YTM is greater than coupon rate, and coupon rate is greater than current yield

explanation.text: The Logic: For a premium bond, the coupon rate is greater than the current yield, and the current yield is greater than YTM. For Bond A: coupon rate is 9% on face value of Rs. 100, current yield is Rs. 9 divided by market price Rs. 104.10, which is about 8.65%, and YTM is lower still because the price must fall from Rs. 104.10 to Rs. 100 at maturity. This pull-to-par effect reduces the total return below the current yield. The Trap: The reverse ordering — coupon rate lower than current yield, lower than YTM — applies to discount bonds, not premium bonds. Note: Remember the premium-bond ordering CR is greater than CY is greater than YTM, and the discount-bond ordering CR is less than CY is less than YTM. The pull-to-par capital loss on a premium bond is what drags YTM below the current yield.
